qualifying_updates.title: Reviewing AI-Generated Code with Difftastic
qualifying_updates.summary: OpenReplay published a workflow for reviewing AI-generated commits with Difftastic, using AST-based diffs to suppress formatting churn and reveal behavior-changing edits. The article recommends targeting exact agent commits with git external diff output and using difft --check-only --exit-code as a pre-merge or CI gate for distinguishing semantic changes from pure reformatting.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: Agent-generated branches often mix formatting churn with real logic edits. Structural diff review is a concrete coding-practice and source-workflow control that can reduce reviewer fatigue, make AI-authored behavior changes auditable, and provide a narrow verification gate before merge.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Consider an AI-diff review pattern that asks agents to isolate behavior changes, lets reviewers inspect exact commits with structural diffs, and treats parser fallback as a signal requiring ordinary textual review.
follow_up_notes: If ingested later, create or update a local practice note about structural diff review for AI-authored commits rather than a broad Difftastic product page.
Check whether existing source-workflow pages already mention semantic diff gates before synthesizing.

qualifying_updates.title: Meta to take on Anthropic's Claude and OpenAI's Codex with new coding agent
qualifying_updates.visible_date_basis: Article page exposes an ISO timestamp in the article header.
qualifying_updates.summary: Business Insider reported that Meta announced a beta coding agent called Muse Code, powered by Muse Spark 1.2, positioned as a lower-cost competitor to Claude Code and OpenAI Codex. The report notes a discounted contributor tier whose condition is that user activity can be used to improve Meta products, while companies working with proprietary code may prefer a standard tier.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: The broad product launch belongs upstream, but the pricing and contributor-tier terms are a local governance signal: team adoption playbooks should distinguish low-cost coding-agent tiers from proprietary-code-safe tiers, and should require explicit data-use checks before allowing repository access.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Record only a downstream governance note: coding-agent tier selection should include explicit checks for training, feedback, telemetry, retention, proprietary-code handling, and per-team budget controls.
follow_up_notes: Route any durable Muse Code product/entity coverage to the upstream AI wiki.
If ingested locally, synthesize only into governance/adoption pages as a data-use and cost-tier review example.
